idiom_name: Optional<Wrapped> with if let / guard let, ?. and ??
implementation_notes: Swift's Optional<Wrapped> is an enum with cases some(Wrapped) and none, usually written T?, and the only routes to the payload are unwrapping: optional binding (if let, guard let, switch), optional chaining (?.), nil-coalescing (??), or the forced unwrap ! which traps at run time - all documented on the Optional type. No Maybe class is idiomatic; Optional is already the shape of dictionary subscripts, failable initializers such as Int("42"), and weak/delegate references. map and flatMap transform when a value is present, and Optional is a real type in the module, so it can appear in containers and generic positions.
pitfalls: Forced unwraps (!) and implicitly unwrapped optionals (T!) trap on nil; each one is a crash the type system was meant to remove, so keep IUOs to outlets and ! to proven invariants.
guard let exits early while if let nests a scope: mixing both in long functions obscures which absence path ran - one style per function keeps it readable.
Optional<Optional<T>> is expressible in Swift, and ?? / flatMap collapse levels silently, so double wrapping usually signals a modelling mistake rather than a domain distinction.
In collections, map with a closure returning T? produces nested optionals; flatMap/compactMap is the documented fix.
